Tales and Folklore

Old Deccan Days

Or Hindoo Fairy Legends current in Southern India

Mary Frere; narrated by Anna Liberata de Souza

Twenty-four fairy legends of the Deccan told by Anna Liberata de Souza to Mary Frere (1868), often called the first book of Indian folk tales collected in English.

docs.title: About this book
docs.text:
Mary Frere (1845–1911) wrote down these tales in the 1860s from her ayah, Anna Liberata de Souza, a Christian woman of Lingayat descent who had learnt them from her grandmother: Punchkin, whose life was hidden in a parrot, Little Surya Bai, the Wanderings of Vicram Maharajah, the Brahman, the Tiger and the Six Judges. The narrator’s own story of her life is printed with them. First published in 1868; this is the text of the edition of 1898, with an introduction by Sir Bartle Frere.

From Wikisource · Public domain

Mary Frere (1845–1911), Old Deccan Days (1868; edition of 1898), the tales narrated by Anna Liberata de Souza, as transcribed on English Wikisource by its contributors.
